finding: src/anomaly/_signal_projection.py:139 Verified projection can be replaced between verification and query.
rationale: The blocker survives because the exact checkpoint exposes an unsynchronized public rebuild that can replace the verified pathname before read_rows reopens it, so a completed canonical-input update and rebuild can make search_signals return projection-B rows while retaining projection-A's manifest identity without any fail-closed post-read check, directly violating the required input-hash binding and stale-projection rejection.

evidence.output: At the locked checkpoint, build_projection writes staged artifacts and independently replaces signals.duckdb at line 93 and its manifest at line 94; verified_projection hashes the current database at line 139 but returns only Path plus manifest at line 143; read_rows later opens that path anew at line 155. search_signals obtains the manifest at line 61, calls read_rows only at line 71, and uses that earlier manifest identity for cursor binding at lines 62-66 and 82-83.

evidence.command: Inspect exact-checkpoint synchronization and post-read guards in src/anomaly/_signal_projection.py and src/anomaly/search.py
evidence.output: The exact blobs contain no Lock, RLock, Semaphore, flock, mutex, portalocker, or filelock synchronization; search.py calls verified_projection once, calls read_rows once, and contains zero projection_hash references, so neither synchronization nor a post-read projection-identity/hash check closes the interval.

The canonical producer legitimately updates all bound input families: detector snapshot at lines 698-699, run provenance at line 737, and evidence/signals.jsonl at lines 738-740. After that producer completes, the public build_signal_projection entry point can build and swap a new valid projection during the verified_projection/read_rows gap. Existing tests cover repeatable sequential pagination, sequential stale-input rejection, and a pre-existing symlink only; they provide no concurrent rebuild/read guard.
